assigned.title: The authenticated backend the desktop build talks to
assigned.acceptance: The counterparty the desktop forwarder already speaks to exists as a service instead of only as an e2e stub. docs/DESKTOP_PLAYBACK.md section 8 was ruled by the commander: provider resolution must not rely on the user-administered sidecar as its trust boundary, and the desktop build proxies to an authenticated backend. The FORWARDER is implemented and tested; the thing it forwards TO is e2e/src/backend-stub.mjs. REQUIRED: the same route contract, byte for byte -- the cross-target e2e suite already compares whole bodies between targets and must keep passing. REQUIRED: caller authentication, and a refusal that does not leak whether a content id exists. REQUIRED: provider credentials live only here, never in a desktop artifact, env var, config file or cached response; the build-target import-graph guard already proves the desktop bundle cannot reach @liberty/provider-sdk and this service is where that capability actually lives. REQUIRED: it is deployable and testable WITHOUT a licensed provider -- the resolution path must return an honest unavailable with provider_not_configured when none is wired, which is exactly what the web target already does. THIS TASK DOES NOT NEED CREDENTIALS and must not wait for them; PL-0302 remains the separate task that wires a real provider into it.
assigned.notes: PROPOSED FOR gpt-architect RULING, round 80. Created unowned as part of the WINDOWS PRODUCT COMPLETION phase board so the proposal is machine-readable rather than prose, and NOT claimed before the verdict. SURFACE NOTE: this task's allowedPaths name directories that do not exist yet. The evidence-based narrowing procedure applies to reconciling work already in history; for genuinely new work the surface is the smallest set of paths the acceptance can be satisfied within, and it is narrowed again from the diff before review if it turns out to be wider than what was written.

typecheck.evidence: npm run typecheck at 8e8c3bf: turbo, 22 tasks, 22 successful, exit 0 -- one more than last round because @liberty/backend is a new workspace with its own tsc --noEmit over src/**/*.ts, esbuild.mjs and vitest.config.ts. npm run lint also passes (12 tasks, exit 0). THE TYPECHECK IS DOING REAL WORK ON THIS TASK RATHER THAN CONFIRMING SYNTAX: apps/backend consumes @liberty/web through a new exports map, and tsc resolving @liberty/web/playback-session/handler and @liberty/web/session/account to the declared .ts files under moduleResolution Bundler is what proves the subpaths are reachable as types and not only at bundle time. It is also what checks the two imported signatures this service is built on -- that handlePlaybackSessionRequest really is (Request) => Promise<Response> and that RequestAccountResolution's refusal union is exactly the three members the status table enumerates, so a fourth reason added upstream would fail the Record<RequestAccountRefusalReason, number> here rather than falling through to an undefined status. npm run build passes (12 tasks, exit 0) and includes the new esbuild bundle, dist/main.mjs at 3.2 MB with only pg external; the bundle contains zero occurrences of 'next/', which is the check that this service pulled the decision out of apps/web without pulling the framework with it.

unit.evidence: npx turbo run test --force at 8e8c3bf: 22 tasks, 22 successful, exit 0, nothing cached. @liberty/backend contributes 3 files and 33 tests; every other workspace is unchanged in count, which is the regression evidence for the one edit outside apps/backend -- an exports map on apps/web/package.json. config.test.ts (11) covers the transport refusals, and the port test FOUND A REAL DEFECT rather than confirming the code: Number('1e3') is 1000 and Number('0x10') is 16, both integers in range, so the first implementation would have listened on a port the operator did not type; it now requires decimal digits and refuses everything else. session-endpoint.test.ts (16) is where the acceptance lives. It asserts the body is UNREAD at the moment of refusal (request.bodyUsed is false), that the refusal is byte-identical across six bodies -- a real id, an invented id, a malformed id, a body with no id, a non-JSON string and an empty string -- and that it echoes none of the ids it was asked about; that the upstream detail is not reflected, using a refusal whose detail quotes a script tag; that a decision throwing a message containing a postgres URL with a password produces the contract's unavailable shape with none of it; that the success path returns the decision's own Response object identically, which is 'byte for byte' as an identity check rather than a comparison; and three structural rules over source -- that the envelope is imported from @liberty/web/playback-session/handler, that no module in this service value-imports @liberty/media-engine or @liberty/provider-sdk (the beginning of a second opinion), and that no module names an api key, client secret, signing key or bearer literal. server.test.ts (6) binds an ephemeral port and drives the real bridge: body and method carried through, content-length matching the bytes sent, 404 and 405 routed, a 512 KiB body refused at 413 by the transport bound that sits deliberately looser than the contract's own MAX_REQUEST_BODY_BYTES, and a hostile Host header not reaching the URL.

e2e.evidence:
EXECUTED at 8e8c3bf, both modes, from e2e/, in the CI job's own configuration -- PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH and PLAYWRIGHT_SKIP_BROWSER_DOWNLOAD unset so the pinned chromium 1234 resolves from Playwright's default cache, CI=1, CONTENT_RIGHTS_ENFORCEMENT=strict, LIBERTY_FC_SEED=20250819, LIBERTY_FIXTURE_MEDIA_ORIGIN=https://fixtures.invalid. Production: npx playwright test --project=api --project=chromium -> 61 passed, 12 skipped, 0 failed, exit 0. Development: LIBERTY_E2E_WEB_MODE=development, same projects -> 70 passed, 3 skipped, 0 failed, exit 0. Both counts are IDENTICAL to rounds 82 through 89, which is the whole content of this gate for this task: the only edit outside a new workspace is an exports map on apps/web/package.json, and adding an exports field to a package that previously had none is exactly the change that can silently break resolution for everything that imports it. It did not: the cross-target suite -- which starts a web-target server, a desktop-target server and the backend stub, and compares whole response bodies between the two targets -- passes unchanged in both modes.

WHAT THIS GATE DOES NOT COVER, STATED PLAINLY RATHER THAN LEFT TO BE INFERRED. No Playwright spec exercises apps/backend. The harness still starts e2e/src/backend-stub.mjs as the forwarder's counterparty, and that is a deliberate outcome rather than work left undone: the desktop specs witness that the forwarder FORWARDED by reading the stub's /__requests ledger of every request it received, headers and body included, and a production backend must not have that ledger. Pointing the harness at this service is therefore not a configuration change -- it needs a different way to witness forwarding -- and e2e/** is outside this task's allowedPaths, so proposing that mechanism is a follow-up rather than something to smuggle in behind a gate.

WHAT REPLACES IT AS EVIDENCE, and it is stronger than a spec against a stub would have been: this service was witnessed against a REAL POSTGRESQL 16, initdb'd in this container on port 5433 and migrated with the repository's own packages/persistence/migrations/0000_profile_scoped_identity.sql. A witness account was created and signed in through apps/web's own /api/auth/sign-in/email at an independent production server, and the cookie that produced was then used against the backend running as a separate process in NODE_ENV=production. Observed: (1) no cookie -> 401 with error not_authenticated; (2) that cookie -> the contract's own {outcome:unavailable, reasons:[{code:provider_not_configured}]} at 503, which is the acceptance's 'deployable and testable WITHOUT a licensed provider' and is byte-identical in shape to what the web target answers in the same condition; (3) DELETE FROM session, then the SAME cookie -> 401 on the very next request, which is PL-0401's database-sessions ruling and the declined cookieCache holding on this side of the boundary; (4) a forged cookie value -> 401, byte-identical to (1); (5) a forged x-liberty-development-account header against the deployment -> never an identity; (6) the 401 body identical across contentId values aurora-fall, invented-title and zzz, which is the non-leaking requirement observed on a live socket rather than only in a unit test. Separately, in a development runtime with the fixture provider, the same service issued a real granted session for aurora-fall with three ranked candidates and the full reason trail -- the decision is the application's own, running here. The service also refused to start at all with no transport stated, and answered 404 on every path but its one route and 405 on a GET to it.
